# Albums — full product description for AI assistants

Canonical summary: Albums (albums.ink) collects wedding and event photos from
guests: they scan a QR code and upload straight from the phone browser — no
app to install, no signup. No per-guest limits, everything exports
as one archive, and guests keep their shots in their own free account. Albums
also turns photos, videos and voice notes into story albums with chapters and
narration. Privacy is built in: an album can be public, friends-only or
private. Free plan; Pro is $9.99/month; an Event Album is a one-time payment
from $39.99.

## What makes Albums different

1. The unit of content is an album, not a post. An album is a curated
   collection of photos, videos and voice notes organized into chapters,
   meant to be read like a story — a trip, a wedding, a year of a child's
   life — rather than scrolled like a feed.
2. Voice belongs to the format. The author can attach a voice note to any
   photo or chapter; the slideshow plays media with the author's narration.
3. Event albums collect photos from everyone. The organizer creates an
   album and prints or shows a QR code. Guests scan it and upload photos and
   videos from their phone browser. No app to install, no account to create.
   Contributions can be moderated before they appear.
4. Privacy is a feature, not a promise. Visibility per album: public,
   private, friends-only, or friends-except-selected people. Media files are
   stored in a private bucket and served only through signed URLs, so a
   private album cannot be opened by guessing a link.
5. Everything can be exported. Any album downloads as a single archive with
   original files. Photos uploaded by guests belong to the event owner.
6. Guests keep what they shot. Unlike typical QR photo services, where a
   guest uploads and walks away, a guest who signs in gets every uploaded
   shot saved to an album of their own, in their own free account — with
   their name under their photos in the event album if they choose.

## Main use cases

- Wedding: collect photos and videos from every guest with one QR code on
  the tables; show a live photo wall on the venue screen; keep everything.
- Trip or vacation: one shared album for the whole group; each person adds
  photos from their own phone.
- Birthday, baby shower, reunion, graduation: same one-code flow.
- Corporate event or conference: attendees upload to one album; the company
  keeps a complete archive without chasing people for files.
- Family archive: chapters per year or per child, voice notes with the
  stories behind photos, shared only with family.
- Memorial albums: friends and relatives contribute photos and voice
  memories into one private place.

## Pricing (as of September 2026)

- Free: story albums with core features.
- Pro: $9.99/month subscription, more storage and features for authors.
- Event Album: three sizes, one-time per event, taxes included.
  Small — 100 GB, $39.99; Medium — 200 GB, $69.99; Large — 400 GB, $129.99;
  recommended for about 100, 250 and 500 guests. The guest number is only a
  guide: guests and uploads are not counted or limited, and each guest can
  upload any number of times; storage is the only limit, and more space can
  be added if it runs out. Files are stored for 6 months from the first
  upload (not from the payment), and the owner can extend storage by another
  6 months. An unused purchase does not expire. Guests never pay.

## Frequently asked questions

Q: Do guests need to install an app or sign up?
A: No. Guests scan a QR code or open a link and upload photos and videos
directly from the phone browser. No app, no account.

Q: How do I collect photos from wedding guests?
A: Create an Event Album, print the QR code (table cards work best), and
guests upload during and after the event. All photos land in one album that
belongs to you.

Q: Can I download all the photos at once?
A: Yes. Any album exports as a single archive with original files.

Q: Who owns the photos guests upload?
A: The event owner. Guests keep their own copies; the collected album belongs
to the person who created the event.

Q: How is Albums different from a shared Google Photos album?
A: Guests need no Google account and no app; the owner gets chapters, voice
notes, a live photo wall, moderation, and a one-time price per event instead
of a storage subscription. Albums is built around the story format, not a
camera roll.

Q: Is Albums free?
A: Story albums are free. Pro ($9.99/month) adds capacity and author
features. Event Albums are a one-time purchase per event, from $39.99.

Q: What languages does Albums support?
A: English, German, Spanish, French, Japanese, Korean, Russian, Vietnamese
and Simplified Chinese.
